title: Hagelloch 1861: the prodrome in two parts, how infectious each part is fitted with the probabilities

source.citation: Measles in Hagelloch, Germany, 1861: 188 children, from Pfeilsticker (1863) as reanalysed by Oesterle (1992), in the outbreaks R package 1.9.0 (measles_hagelloch_1861); examples/hagelloch-1861/cases.json in this repository.

evidence.quote: date_of_prodrome and infector, for 184 of the 188 children
evidence.working: For each child with an infector, the days from the infector's prodrome to the child's own: 7 to 16, median 10 (184 pairs; 10 in school-class pairs, 11 in household pairs). The child was infected at some point in the infector's infectious days; a classmate only in the prodrome, when the infector was at school. Taking the middle of the infector's prodrome as the day of infection gives 6 days (10th centile), 8.5 (median) and 10.5 to 11 (90th) in each kind of pair. No single number fits: of the 68 class pairs, at most 41 allow any one value. 6 to 11 days, drawn evenly, has the median's mean of 8.5.
evidence.note: The infector column is each child's putative source, as the record gives it, not an observed transmission. The Pink Book's 10 days lies inside this range, toward its top.

evidence.quote: date_of_prodrome and date_of_rash, for all 188 children
evidence.working: Days from the prodrome to the rash: 0 to 13, 10th centile 2, median 4, 90th 6, mean 3.95; 72 children had 4. 2 to 6 days, drawn evenly, has a mean of 4.
evidence.note: The record's prodrome of 2 to 6 days, mean 4, split as 1 to 4 early days and 1 to 2 late ones: the same mean. The split itself is assumed; nothing in the record marks it.

evidence.quote: transmissible from 4 days before through 4 days after rash onset
evidence.working: The day of the rash and the 4 days after it: 5 days. With the 4-day prodrome, 9 infectious days in all, as in the Pink Book set.
evidence.note: Not in the record: nothing marks when a child stopped being infectious. Kept from the Pink Book.

evidence.working: Fitted 2026-11-21 by scripts/abm-hagelloch-fit.mjs --split: the three probabilities and the two weights together, on a grid of 5 × 6 × 5 × 4 × 4 points at 100 runs each, then 7 × 7 × 7 × 3 × 3 around the best at 300; the Poisson deviance of the record's rashes per day (days 0 to 89 from the index child's) against the model's mean, the school shut on Sundays. Best 0.33; within 4 of the best's deviance, 0.08 to 0.33.
